source_text: Ad omnes aetates - dixi - pertinere illud, de quo Apostolus loquitur, beneficium Dei: Qui eruit nos de potestate tenebrarum, et transtulit in regnum Filii caritatis suae Fidem non dubitare christianam, quam novi haeretici oppugnare coeperunt, et eos qui lavacro regenerationis abluuntur, redimi de diaboli potestate; et eos qui nondum tali regeneratione redempti sunt, etiam parvulos filios redemptorum, sub eiusdem diaboli esse potestate captivos, nisi et ipsi eadem gratia redimantur
pass_a_gloss: To all aetates - dixi - pertinere that, about/from whither apostle loquitur, beneficium of-God: who eruit we about/from by-power tenebrarum, and transtulit in kingdom sons caritatis his-own faith not dubitare christianam, than/which novi heretics oppugnare coeperunt, and them who by-washing of-regeneration abluuntur, redimi about/from of-the-devil by-power; and them who not-yet tali regeneration redempti are, also parvulos sons redemptorum, under eiusdem of-the-devil to-be by-power captivos, unless and themselves the-same grace redimantur.

lemmas.lexica: LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS parvulus; Blaise infants in original-sin debate

pass_b_english: You tried to stir up the crowd against me.
Forgetting our single combat, you took refuge in the crowd.
With a treaty offered, it was agreed to settle the war, so that our contest would decide everyone’s battles.

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: In the suum cuique definition gratia is partiality, not saving grace.
Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
